objective: Repair AEGIS risk classification, deterministic Codex+Grok reviewer requirements, exact-subject reviewer completeness projection, connector authenticated/lastVerified/lastUsedByRun truth, and founder-readable dashboard explanations, without creating any second authority, store, classifier, or subject-hash path.
constraints: Reuse the existing Registry -> Task Packet -> Gate -> Ledger loop and the existing AEGIS state projector; do not create a parallel authority, store, classifier, or subject-hash implementation

ACCEPTANCE: risk classification for a given diff is deterministic (same subject hash -> same risk tier on repeated runs) and any input it cannot confidently classify renders toward FULL, never toward a lower tier

ACCEPTANCE: the required-reviewer set for a subject is deterministic and always includes Codex and Grok when the packet/risk tier calls for them; a reviewer that is required and missing renders the gate BLOCKED, never silently satisfied

ACCEPTANCE: reviewer completeness is evaluated against the EXACT current subject hash — a review bound to a stale or different subject hash does not count toward completeness, and the projection states which paths are covered, which are missing, and which are stale

ACCEPTANCE: for every connector, the dashboard/state distinguishes three independent facts — authenticated (credential/session valid), lastVerified (timestamp of the last successful health probe), and lastUsedByRun (timestamp/run id of the last time a run actually consumed it) — and none of the three is inferred from another

ACCEPTANCE: authentication alone is never displayed or treated as verification, and verification alone is never displayed or treated as run usage; each fact renders UNAVAILABLE/UNVERIFIED/STALE with its own timestamp when it does not exist, rather than defaulting to a healthy-looking state

ACCEPTANCE: dashboard explanations for risk tier, reviewer completeness, and connector state are written for a non-technical founder reading the page cold — plain language plus the underlying evidence (timestamps, hashes, reviewer names), not internal jargon standing alone
No Vitalis application, protocol, or catalog changes of any kind
No second/parallel authority, evidence store, risk classifier, or subject-hash algorithm; extend the existing ones in place
No n8n integration, reference, or dependency of any kind
No legacy named agents (e.g. retired/renamed workers) reintroduced into routing, registry, or dashboard state
Never store or display credentials, tokens, session identifiers, or raw reviewer transcript contents in code, tests, schema, registry, or dashboard output
GitHub Copilot remains advisory only; it may never satisfy a required-reviewer condition or unblock the gate by itself

Any state this work cannot verify (risk tier, reviewer completeness, connector fact) fails closed toward the stricter/less-available reading — unknown risk renders FULL, unknown reviewer coverage renders incomplete, unknown connector fact renders UNAVAILABLE
Authentication, verification (lastVerified), and run usage (lastUsedByRun) are three distinct claims and this work must not collapse any two of them into one field or one inferred value
Anti-theater: report completion only with changed paths, exact commands run with exit codes, and any UNVERIFIED/UNAVAILABLE item named explicitly in the same response
stopConditions: The fix would require a second authority, evidence store, risk classifier, or subject-hash implementation alongside the existing one
The fix would require touching Vitalis application, protocol, or catalog files
The fix would require reintroducing n8n or a legacy named agent into routing, registry, or dashboard state
Authentication, lastVerified, or lastUsedByRun cannot be made independently true/false/unknown without collapsing them into one signal
A credential, token, session identifier, or raw reviewer transcript would need to be written to a file this packet may touch
Marc issues STOP, delegate, or canon language
